routine: C0/9C37 z-gate + C0/9C5C per-axis collision-commit + C0/9CA1 trigger lookup + C0/9D54 plane update + C0/9D6E conveyor + C0/9DC3 scene-load init. DP=$1D00.
corrections: 9CB7 LDA $7E7080,X is an 8-BIT load (A is 8-bit here: confirmed by 89 80 'BIT #$80' at 9CA4 being a 2-byte 8-bit immediate, and no REP #$20 between 9C89 SEP and 9CB7). The spec calls $7E7080 a '16-bit index plane' with a 'bit15 sentinel' and writes 'int16 idx = (int16)R16_long(0x7E7080 + X)'. WRONG: it reads ONE byte; BMI tests BIT7 of that byte; only that single byte is written to WRMPYA. Correct: uint8 idx = R8_long(0x7E7080 + X); if (idx & 0x80) goto L_9D35; ... WRMPYA = idx;

9DC3 scene-load, party members 2 and 3 OBJ priority: the spec writes ($6E, $6F) to ($0C00+p1,$0C01+p1) and ($0C00+p2,$0C01+p2). WRONG. The accumulator is loaded with $6F at 9E09 and NEVER reloaded; party2 (9E11/9E14) and party3 (9E1A/9E1D) both store A=$6F into BOTH their $0C00 and $0C01 priority bytes. Only the PLAYER (9E06=$6E, 9E0B=$6F) gets the ($6E,$6F) pair.

9AC8/9AD1 support comment: 'A := (A & $1E) [mask cellX into 0x40 stride]' understates it. The AND $1E runs in 16-bit A mode (REP #$20 at 9ACA) so it is a 16-bit AND of the full accumulator $69:$67 (cellY:cellX) against the 16-bit dp operand $1F:$1E (Ymask:Xmask), yielding index (($69&$1F)<<8)|($67&$1E) -- identical to the trigger-lookup de-interleave. Not a single-byte cellX mask.

9C70 prose imprecision (C code is fine): the comment says Y-vel 'bit15 set -> negative / moving up'. The instruction is BIT #$0080 (3-byte 16-bit immediate, confirmed), which tests BIT7 of the 16-bit value, not the bit15 sign bit. The spec's C mask 'R16($30) & 0x0080' is correct; only the explanatory gloss is wrong.
